label: Acts 20:1
text: After the uproar had ceased, Paul sent for the disciples, took leave of them, and departed to go into Macedonia.

label: Acts 20:2
text: When he had gone through those parts, and had encouraged them with many words, he came into Greece.

label: Acts 20:3
text: When he had spent three months there, and a plot was made against him by Jews as he was about to set sail for Syria, he determined to return through Macedonia.

label: Acts 20:4
text: These accompanied him as far as Asia: Sopater of Beroea; Aristarchus and Secundus of the Thessalonians; Gaius of Derbe; Timothy; and Tychicus and Trophimus of Asia.

label: Acts 20:5
text: But these had gone ahead, and were waiting for us at Troas.

label: Acts 20:6
text: We sailed away from Philippi after the days of Unleavened Bread, and came to them at Troas in five days, where we stayed seven days.

label: Acts 20:7
text: On the first day of the week, when the disciples were gathered together to break bread, Paul talked with them, intending to depart on the next day, and continued his speech until midnight.

label: Acts 20:8
text: There were many lights in the upper room where we were gathered together.

label: Acts 20:9
text: A certain young man named Eutychus sat in the window, weighed down with deep sleep. As Paul spoke still longer, being weighed down by his sleep, he fell down from the third floor, and was taken up dead.

label: Acts 20:10
text: Paul went down, and fell upon him, and embracing him said, “Don’t be troubled, for his life is in him.”

label: Acts 20:11
text: When he had gone up, and had broken bread, and eaten, and had talked with them a long while, even until break of day, he departed.

label: Acts 20:12
text: They brought the boy in alive, and were greatly comforted.

label: Acts 20:13
text: But we, going ahead to the ship, set sail for Assos, intending to take Paul aboard there; for he had so arranged, intending himself to go by land.

label: Acts 20:14
text: When he met us at Assos, we took him aboard, and came to Mitylene.

label: Acts 20:15
text: Sailing from there, we came the following day opposite Chios. The next day we touched at Samos and stayed at Trogyllium, and the day after we came to Miletus.

variants.reading: omits 'and stayed at Trogyllium' (και μειναντες εν Τρωγυλλιω)
variants.note: The phrase is present in D (Codex Bezae), uncial 049 and the Byzantine majority; the Alexandrian texts omit it (Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Acts of the Apostles').

label: Acts 20:16
text: For Paul had determined to sail past Ephesus, that he might not have to spend time in Asia; for he was hastening, if it were possible for him, to be in Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost.

label: Acts 20:17
text: From Miletus he sent to Ephesus, and called to himself the elders of the assembly.

label: Acts 20:18
text: When they had come to him, he said to them, “You yourselves know, from the first day that I set foot in Asia, how I was with you all the time,

label: Acts 20:19
text: serving the Lord with all humility, with many tears, and with trials which happened to me by the plots of the Jews;

label: Acts 20:20
text: how I didn’t shrink from declaring to you anything that was profitable, teaching you publicly and from house to house,

label: Acts 20:21
text: testifying both to Jews and to Greeks repentance toward God, and faith toward our Lord Jesus.

label: Acts 20:22
text: Now, behold, I go bound by the Spirit to Jerusalem, not knowing what will happen to me there;

label: Acts 20:23
text: except that the Holy Spirit testifies in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions wait for me.

label: Acts 20:24
text: But these things don’t count; nor do I hold my life dear to myself, so that I may finish my race with joy, and the ministry which I received from the Lord Jesus, to fully testify to the Good News of the grace of God.

label: Acts 20:25
text: “Now, behold, I know that you all, among whom I went about preaching God’s Kingdom, will see my face no more.

label: Acts 20:26
text: Therefore I testify to you today that I am clean from the blood of all men,

label: Acts 20:27
text: for I didn’t shrink from declaring to you the whole counsel of God.

label: Acts 20:28
text: Take heed, therefore, to yourselves, and to all the flock, in which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers, to shepherd the assembly of the Lord and God which he purchased with his own blood.

variants.note: Sinaiticus and Vaticanus read 'church of God'; P74, A, C*, D, E and the majority read 'church of the Lord' or 'church of the Lord and God' (Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Acts of the Apostles').

variants.reading: εκκλησιαν του κυριου ('church of the Lord')
variants.note: P74 reads 'church of the Lord'; the WEB's 'assembly of the Lord and God' is the Byzantine reading (Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Acts of the Apostles').

label: Acts 20:29
text: For I know that after my departure, vicious wolves will enter in among you, not sparing the flock.

label: Acts 20:30
text: Men will arise from among your own selves, speaking perverse things, to draw away the disciples after them.

label: Acts 20:31
text: Therefore watch, remembering that for a period of three years I didn’t cease to admonish everyone night and day with tears.

label: Acts 20:32
text: Now, brothers, I entrust you to God, and to the word of his grace, which is able to build up, and to give you the inheritance among all those who are sanctified.

label: Acts 20:33
text: I coveted no one’s silver, or gold, or clothing.

label: Acts 20:34
text: You yourselves know that these hands served my necessities, and those who were with me.

label: Acts 20:35
text: In all things I gave you an example, that so laboring you ought to help the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, that he himself said, ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’”

label: Acts 20:36
text: When he had spoken these things, he knelt down and prayed with them all.

label: Acts 20:37
text: They all wept a lot, and fell on Paul’s neck and kissed him,

label: Acts 20:38
text: sorrowing most of all because of the word which he had spoken, that they should see his face no more. And they accompanied him to the ship.

label: After the Ephesian uproar Paul departed for Macedonia and encouraged the disciples
statement: After the uproar had ceased, Paul sent for the disciples, took leave of them, and departed to go into Macedonia, going through those parts and encouraging them with many words.

label: Paul spent three months in Greece, and a Jewish plot made him return through Macedonia instead of sailing for Syria
statement: Paul came into Greece (Achaia) and spent three months there; as he was about to set sail for Syria, a plot of the Jews made him determine to return through Macedonia.
note: Greece here is the Roman senatorial province of Achaia.

label: Seven named companions accompanied Paul as far as Asia
statement: Sopater of Beroea, Aristarchus and Secundus of the Thessalonians, Gaius of Derbe, Timothy, and Tychicus and Trophimus of Asia accompanied him as far as Asia.
note: The only New Testament list naming the travelling delegates of the collection churches; the men of 19:29 (Gaius, Aristarchus) reappear in part.

label: Aristarchus the companion was of the Thessalonians
statement: Aristarchus, one of the two 'of the Thessalonians' in the companion list, was a man of Thessalonica in Macedonia.
note: Acts 19:29 already names him among Paul's Macedonian companions.

label: The party sailed from Philippi to Troas in five days and stayed seven days
statement: The companions had gone ahead and waited at Troas; the narrating party sailed away from Philippi after the days of unleavened bread and came to them at Troas in five days, and stayed seven days.
note: Second visit to Troas; the first was Acts 16:8-11 (three days then).

label: The departure from Philippi fell immediately after the days of unleavened bread
statement: The sailing from Philippi took place after the days of unleavened bread (the Passover festival week).
note: The same festival calendar as Acts 12:3-4 and Mark 14:12; related_to links, since those claims are the specific events of Acts 12 and the Markan Passover usage.

label: On the first day of the week the disciples gathered to break bread and Paul spoke until midnight
statement: On the first day of the week the disciples at Troas were gathered together to break bread, and Paul, intending to depart the next day, talked with them and continued his speech until midnight.
note: The gathering began on Saturday evening (Jewish reckoning, evening first); 'the first day of the week' translates tē mia tōn sabbatōn.

label: Many lamps burned in the upper room where they were gathered
statement: There were many lights (lamps) in the upper room where they were gathered together at Troas.
note: An upper room (hyperoon) with many lamps lighting a night meeting.

label: Eutychus fell from the third floor and was taken up dead; Paul embraced him and the boy was brought in alive
statement: A young man named Eutychus, sitting in the window and sinking into deep sleep as Paul spoke still longer, fell down from the third floor and was taken up dead; Paul went down, embraced him and said 'his life is in him', and the boy was brought in alive, and they were greatly comforted.
note: Miracle claim; searched honestly and recorded none-found. Eutychus is a common Greek name of the period (Wikipedia 'Acts 20').

label: The ship went on to Assos while Paul went by land; they took him aboard and came to Mitylene
statement: The narrating party sailed ahead from Troas for Assos intending to take Paul aboard there, for he had arranged to go by land; when he met them at Assos they took him aboard and came to Mitylene.
note: Assos lies about 30 km south of Troas; the land route cut across the cape the ship had to double.

label: From Mitylene the ship passed Chios, touched at Samos, stayed at Trogyllium and came to Miletus
statement: Sailing from Mitylene, they came the following day opposite Chios, the next day touched at Samos and stayed at Trogyllium, and the day after came to Miletus.
note: Island-hopping coastal route down the Ionian coast; the Trogyllium clause is a textual variant (see the passage).

label: Paul decided to sail past Ephesus, hastening to be at Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost
statement: Paul had determined to sail past Ephesus so as not to spend time in Asia, for he was hastening, if possible, to be at Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost.
note: Pentecost, the feast fifty days after Passover (Acts 2:1), used as a travel deadline.

label: From Miletus Paul sent to Ephesus and summoned the elders of the assembly
statement: From Miletus Paul sent to Ephesus and called to himself the elders (presbyteroi) of the assembly.
note: Miletus is about 40 miles south of Ephesus (Wikipedia 'Acts 20'); the elders are called overseers (episkopoi) in verse 28.

label: Paul reminded the Ephesian elders of three years of admonition night and day
statement: Paul told the elders to remember that for a period of three years he did not cease to admonish everyone night and day with tears.
note: Acts 19:8-10 reports three months in the synagogue and two years in the hall of Tyrannus; 20:31 rounds the whole Ephesian ministry to three years.

label: Paul told the elders that his own hands served his necessities and his companions'
statement: Paul said he coveted no one's silver, gold or clothing, and that these hands served his necessities and those who were with him.
note: The artisan self-support Paul also reports in 1 Thessalonians 2:9 and 2 Thessalonians 3:8 (biblical cross-reference, not evidence).

label: Sopater of Beroea
note: Of Beroea in Macedonia (Acts 20:4); the name is sometimes connected with Sosipater of Romans 16:21. No source outside the New Testament names him.

label: Aristarchus of Thessalonica
note: Of Thessalonica (Acts 20:4); seized with Gaius at the Ephesian riot (19:29), later 'fellow prisoner' in Colossians 4:10 and Philemon 24. A Thessalonian inscription names 'Aristarchus son of Aristarchus, a politarch' but its date (39/38 BC?) is decades before Acts.

label: Secundus of Thessalonica
note: Named in Acts 20:4 only; no source outside the New Testament names him.

label: Gaius of Derbe
note: Of Derbe (Acts 20:4). A man named Gaius was seized at Ephesus (19:29) and a Gaius of Corinth is named in Romans 16:23 and 1 Corinthians 1:14; whether these are one man or two or three is disputed. No external source names any of them.

label: Tychicus
note: Of the province of Asia (Acts 20:4); the letter-bearer named in Ephesians 6:21-22 and Colossians 4:7-8. No source outside the New Testament names him.

label: Trophimus the Ephesian
note: A companion of Paul from Ephesus (named also at Acts 20:4); the Asian Jews had seen him with Paul in Jerusalem (21:29); no independent source names him.

label: Eutychus
note: The young man of Troas who fell from the third-floor window while Paul spoke (Acts 20:9); a common Greek name of the period. No source outside the New Testament names him.

label: Macedonia (Roman province)
note: The Roman province recreated in 146 BC; Paul's Macedonian field (Acts 16-20).

label: Greece (Achaia)
note: 'Greece' in Acts 20:2-3 is the Roman senatorial province of Achaia, separated from Macedonia in 27 BC, capital Corinth.

label: Assos
note: Ancient Greek city in the Troad, where Paul rejoined the ship (Acts 20:13-14); inscribed on the UNESCO Tentative List in 2017.

label: Mitylene (Mytilene)
note: Chief city and harbor of Lesbos, the first stop after Assos (Acts 20:14).

label: Chios
note: Ionian island the ship passed on the leg from Mitylene (Acts 20:15); one of the twelve Ionian League members and an early coin-minting city.

label: Samos
note: Island the ship touched (Acts 20:15); home of Pythagoreion and the Heraion, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

label: Trogyllium (promontory of Mycale)
note: Mainland cape opposite Samos, a spur of Mount Mycale; the anchorage named in some texts of Acts 20:15 and omitted in the Alexandrian witnesses. Coordinates approximate.

label: Miletus
note: Influential ancient Greek city on the Maeander mouth; its harbor, protected by the island of Lade, later silted up - by the Roman era neighbouring Priene and Myus had already lost theirs. Paul's ship put in here and the elders met him (Acts 20:15-17).

label: Miletus — the excavated ancient city
excavators: Olivier Rayet (1873); Julius Hülsen and Theodor Wiegand (1899-1931); Carl Weickart (1938, 1955-1957); Ruhr University Bochum today
periods: Bronze Age, Archaic, Classical, Hellenistic, Roman, Byzantine
note: Excavated since 1873; the Market Gate of Miletus was reassembled in Berlin's Pergamon Museum. The city's silted harbor explains why the ship anchored off Miletus while the elders came out from Ephesus.

label: Thessalonian inscription of Aristarchus son of Aristarchus, politarch
note: Greek inscription naming 'Aristarchus son of Aristarchus, a politarch of Thessalonica'; Wikipedia notes it 'may be the same person' as Paul's companion, which is conjecture, and the date is decades before Acts 20.

label: Strabo's distance from the Trogilian promontory to Samos
method: Strabo states 'The distance from the Trogilian promontory to Samos is forty stadia' - about 7.2 km at the 180 m stadion, a strait 'about seven stadia in width' between Mycale and Samos.

excerpt: The province was created in 146 BC, after the Roman general Quintus Caecilius Metellus defeated Andriscus of Macedon, the last self-styled King of Macedonia in the Fourth Macedonian War.

label: Wikipedia: Achaia (Roman province)
title: Achaia (Roman province)
excerpt: Achaia was a senatorial province, thus free from military men and legions, and one of the most prestigious and sought-after provinces for senators to govern.

label: Wikipedia: Roman Syria

excerpt: Roman Syria was an early Roman province annexed to the Roman Republic in 64 BCE by Pompey in the Third Mithridatic War.

label: Wikipedia: Assos
title: Assos
excerpt: The Acts of the Apostles [ 3 ] also refers to visits to the city by Luke the Evangelist and Paul the Apostle. [ 4 ] Today, Assos is a holiday retreat amid ancient ruins. In 2017 it was inscribed on the UNESCO Tentative list of World Heritage Sites in Turkey.

label: Wikipedia: Mytilene
title: Mytilene
excerpt: As an ancient city, lying off the east coast, Mytilene was initially confined to a small island just offshore that later was joined to Lesbos, creating a north and south harbor.

label: Wikipedia: Chios
title: Chios
excerpt: Chios was one of the original twelve member states of the Ionian League. As a result, Chios, at the end of the 7th century BC, [ 25 ] was one of the first cities to strike or mint coins, establishing the sphinx as its symbol.

label: Wikipedia: Samos
title: Samos
excerpt: Samos was an especially rich and powerful city-state, particularly known for its vineyards and wine production. [ 6 ] It is home to Pythagoreion and the Heraion of Samos, a UNESCO World Heritage Site that includes the Eupalinian aqueduct, a marvel of ancient engineering.

label: Wikipedia: Trogyllium
title: Trogyllium
excerpt: It is mentioned in some versions of Acts 20:15, as a place where Luke the Evangelist, Paul the Apostle and their companions stayed during their southbound maritime journey from Assos to Rhodes. The King James Version and the Geneva Bible mention this stop-over point

label: Wikipedia: Miletus (excavations and harbor)

excerpt: The first excavations in Miletus were conducted by the French archaeologist Olivier Rayet in 1873, followed by the German archaeologists Julius Hülsen and Theodor Wiegand [ 32 ] [ 33 ] [ 34 ] between 1899 and 1931.
